chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Shaybani, and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad (may Allah be pleased with them) said: We were told by Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan, who said: We were told by Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, who said: We were told by Tamim ibn Buhlul, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from Abdullah ibn Fadl al-Hashimi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah Ja'ar ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)

about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He whom Allah guides, he is certainly the guided, and he whom He leads astray, you will certainly not find for him a protecting guide.» So he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, makes the aberrant go astray, on the Day of Resurrection, from the Home of His Generosity and guides the people of faith and good deed to His Paradise
like how He, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: «And Allah leads the aberrant astray and does what He wishes.»
Also, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: «Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith. Under them will rivers flow in the Gardens of Bliss.»

He said: Then I said: And His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And my success is not but through Allah» and His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «If Allah supports you, then none can overcome you, and if He abandons you, then who is there to support you after Him»?

So he said: If the servant does what Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, commands him of obedience, his act will be in accordance to the commandment of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and by it, a servant will be considered as being given success. And if the servant would want to enter into something of disobedience to Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, between him and the act of disobedience and then abandons it, his abandonment of it would be by being given success from Allah, Exalted is He. And whenever He would apart from between him and the act of disobedience and not interfere between him and it until he performs it, then He has abandoned him, not supported him nor given him success.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine guidance and leading astray in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the interplay between divine decree and human agency, defining 'guidance' and 'leading astray' as Allah's active direction of the faithful to Paradise and the unjust away from His grace. He further clarifies that 'success' (tawfiq) is the divine enablement for obedience, while 'abandonment' (khal') is the withholding of that support, allowing the servant to persist in sin until they commit it. This explanation underscores the Shia understanding of *fay'* (divine facilitation) as a conditional gift dependent on the servant's readiness to act.
